Minesweeper on NoCharge — a calm clearing loop, not a speed run

Current NoCharge Minesweeper is a nine-by-nine, ten-mine board with first-square safety, optional flags, no chord action, and no timer or saved best time.

By NoCharge Editorial·Reviewed by NoCharge Editorial·Published August 27, 2026·Updated November 24, 2026·2 min read
Try the detail in a live board.

Clear the field, one safe cell at a time.

Play MinesweeperBrowse all Articles

Bottom line: NoCharge Minesweeper is a nine-by-nine board with ten mines, neighboring counts, optional flags, and no countdown. The first revealed square is guaranteed safe; its surrounding neighbors are not guaranteed safe.

What first-click safety means here

The mine layout is created when the first square is revealed. The engine excludes that selected square from the ten mine positions, then calculates the neighboring counts. It does not reserve an entire safe neighborhood, so the first reveal may show a number rather than opening a large blank area.

Reveal, count, and flag

Each number reports mines in the surrounding eight squares, including diagonals. Flags are optional notes: switch to Flag mode and select a covered square, or use the browser’s context menu on a cell. There is no chord action that automatically reveals neighbors when a flag count matches a number.

The board provides row and column selectors plus a button to reveal or flag the selected square. The cells themselves are standard buttons. The current interface does not document the old F-key and arrow-key shortcuts.

End conditions and records

Opening a mine ends the attempt and displays the mine map. Opening every safe square wins. The scoreboard shows flags placed and safe squares opened; it does not show elapsed time or a best-time record. NoCharge V2 does not save Minesweeper results in browser storage or a score dashboard.

There is no time pressure, but a wrong deduction can still end the board. Treat flags as notes, not proof: the count around each revealed square is the rule to verify.
